_comment: Ore vein definitions. Schema is read by OreConfig::load
(src/apps/world_generator/OreConfig.cpp:26-39): every entry needs
name, min_y, max_y, weight, primary, secondary, sporadic; density is
optional (default 0.5). Block ids are PACKED item ids verified against
src/content/data/registry/items.csv, NOT the constants in OreTypes.h
(that header stops at 10:10 and never defined 10:11-10:19).
Placement rules the generator imposes on these values:
* OreGenerator.cpp:13 picks a vein centre y uniformly from [5, 60],
so a vein outside that range can never be selected. Every band below
intersects [5, 60].
* OreGenerator.cpp:36 selects only veins where min_y <= y <= max_y,
weighted by `weight`.
* OreGenerator.cpp:163-173 paints primary in the core, secondary in the
wing, sporadic only where 3D noise > 0.5.
Band rationale is derived from content already in the repo, not invented:
* diamond_deep_vein is pre-existing and untouched.
* iron_nickel_vein: secondary 10:3 -> 10:14. That slot held copper_ore
(items.csv:268) despite the vein being named for nickel, while 10:14
nickel_ore (items.csv:285) was named by no vein at all. Ids verified
against items.csv, not against OreTypes.h.
* copper_tin_vein: primary 10:0 -> 10:3. Same defect: the vein is named
for copper but its core was iron_ore, and 10:3 copper_ore was placed
ONLY by iron_nickel_vein's buggy slot. Fixing iron_nickel_vein alone
therefore deletes copper from the world, so both slots are corrected
together. iron still leads via iron_nickel_vein.
* sulfur is a fluid-era reagent (chemical_reactor sulfuric acid),
paired with the existing redstone band.
* quartz is a low-banded gangue mineral, paired with the deep band.
* electrum, uranium, platinum, iridium, osmium and chromium are all
rare_materials era (quests.csv 101-113) and are placed mid/deep,
away from the shallow copper/tin band.
* lead, zinc, silver and nickel are common smelt ores and stay in the
mid bands beside the iron vein.
Every band is clamped to [5,60] because that is the range the generator
samples centre y from; the precise depth per ore is a tuning decision,
not a derived constant. tools/reachability_audit.py --veins enforces the
two hard invariants: every registered ore is placed, and no band is dead.

veins.name: bauxite_vein
veins._note: Bauxite is the ALUMINIUM ore - there is no aluminium_ore (gt-4: bauxite -> macerate -> centrifuge/electrolyser yields aluminium dust AND titanium dust). Surface-leaning, matching gt-4's y32-95, clamped to the [5,60] range OreGenerator.cpp:13 samples. titanium_ore rides along as secondary because gt-4 yields titanium from bauxite too.

veins.name: tungsten_vein
veins._note: Deep, rare metal. silicon_ore as secondary: silica-bearing zones carry both.

veins.name: silicon_vein
veins._note: Distinct from quartz_gangue_vein (10:5) on purpose: quartz macerates to quartz, this macerates to silicon_dust. 10 downstream items depend on silicon_dust.
